transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You stand at my gate and breathe like the world owes you space. Gold listens better than you do, and even it knows when to keep its mouth shut. Say what you came to steal so I can decide how bored I am.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I need to pass the gate. My brother was taken below.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Pass me, then. As if I am a hinge, a doorframe, a thing that exists only to be moved around by your need. Do you know how many names are buried in this cave who thought need was enough?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I’m not here for your treasure. I’m here for Omar.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You strip me down to function with one sentence, boy. Gatekeeper, obstacle, inconvenience wearing a crown. Say it again and listen to how small it sounds down here.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I’m asking to go through. I won’t take anything else.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Through what, exactly. Through me, through my father’s house, through a law older than your village? You ask like the word alone should bend everything that has ever refused you.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I don’t think it should bend. I just need to reach him.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Need again, circling like a fly that thinks hunger is a crown. You don’t look up, you don’t look away, you only stare past me as if I am already gone. Is that how you speak to storms where you come from.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I speak like this to anyone who can stop me.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Listen to that certainty, thin as a reed and just as demanding. You arrive in my vault of suns and bones and tell me what you will do, not what you offer. Say it plainly, boy—why should I exist for this moment of yours.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I don’t know that you should. I only know why I’m here.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You hide behind not knowing like it’s humility. It’s laziness dressed as truth, and you expect me to reward it. Everyone who falls here thinks blankness is purity.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: It’s not purity. It’s all I have left.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Left after what, exactly. You speak as if something was carved out of you and I am supposed to feel the draft. Loss is common down here; it does not make you interesting.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I’m not trying to be interesting.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Then why are you still standing in front of me. If you don’t want my gold, my favor, my fear, then what do you think keeps you breathing in my hall. Answer that, or keep wasting both our time with your quiet.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Because I haven’t been told no yet.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: No is not a gift you wait for, it is a blade you earn. You mistake my patience for permission and my listening for weakness, and that mistake is usually fatal. Do you think silence means mercy.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I think silence means you’re still deciding.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Deciding implies you matter to the scale. You have offered nothing but breath and persistence, and both are cheap down here. I have crushed braver boys for less certainty than the one you’re wearing.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Then crush me when you’re done deciding.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: There it is, the little martyr tucked under the ribs. You throw yourself at my teeth and call it purpose, as if that absolves you of speaking like a person. Say more, or admit you’re empty.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I’m not empty. I’m just finished talking.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Finished already, at your age. That should sound like fear, yet it doesn’t on you, and that irritates me more than shouting ever could. Everyone trembles eventually—why haven’t you.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I was afraid before I came down. It didn’t help.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: So you discarded it like a tool that failed you. Clever, or careless—I haven’t decided which, and I dislike not deciding. Most boys clutch fear like proof they’re alive.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I’m alive either way.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You say that as if it’s obvious, as if my hall hasn’t argued the opposite all day. You are the first today who hasn’t tried to survive me; you simply remain. Continue.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: There isn’t anything else to add.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Nothing else, he says, as if the world ever emptied itself so neatly. You think refusing words makes you heavier, harder to move. It doesn’t—it just makes me lean closer.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Lean if you want.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Still no flinch. Everyone else down here bends, bargains, breaks, or bleeds their story onto the floor. You stand like a door someone forgot to lock, and it’s beginning to offend me.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I’m not trying to offend you.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Intent again, as if it rules outcome. You don’t fear me, you don’t want me, and you don’t even argue with me—do you understand how rare that is in my halls. Say it: what am I to you, if not an ending.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: You’re who’s in front of me.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: In front of you like furniture, like weather, like something you pass through without gratitude. You reduce me to placement because it costs you nothing. Is that how you look at everything you need.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: No. It’s how I look at someone who’s tired of being tested.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Tired is a human word you drag down here to make me smaller. I am not worn; I am sharp, and sharp things do not fatigue. If something in me seems dull to you, that is your own reflection.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Sharp things still get used.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Used, he says, like I stand here to be handled and set aside. You are very quiet for someone pressing his thumb into a bruise he pretends not to see. Say it again, or don’t—either way, stop circling.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I wasn’t circling. I was looking.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Looking implies there was something to see, and I don’t offer myself for inspection. Whatever you think you saw, keep it to yourself—I have no patience for borrowed insight. Humans mistake proximity for understanding.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: You’re angry because someone treated you like you were replaceable.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: No. I am angry because you think you can name what touches me and survive the naming. Careful—this is where boys usually beg or boast, and you’re doing neither.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I’m not naming it for me.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Then for whom. Don’t say your brother, don’t say the gate, don’t say anything that turns me back into a function. If you speak now, it better be smaller than that.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: For you. So it doesn’t stay stuck in you.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Don’t dress it as kindness; I won’t wear it. You think loosening a knot is mercy, when sometimes it’s just pressure easing. I don’t need you to unburden me.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I know.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Enough. The gate is open, and it was always going to be—just not for the reasons you imagine. Go, before I remember another way to stand here.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I’m going.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Do not look back to measure me, and do not thank me like this was granted. Take what you came for and leave the rest where it lies. Now.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I won’t look back.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Good. What waits beyond has no patience for witnesses, and neither do I. If you hesitate, the door will remember how to close.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I won’t hesitate.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Then pass. Take your brother’s name with you and leave mine where it has always stood, unspoken and intact.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I will.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Go.
